title: Examining pre-service mathematics teachers' purposes of using ChatGPT in lesson plan development
extended_summary:
This paper examines why pre-service middle school mathematics teachers used ChatGPT while developing lesson plans. The study asks how the tool supported lesson content creation and how it helped participants deepen their own knowledge and address deficiencies during planning.

The intervention/approach was not a classroom teaching intervention but a structured use of ChatGPT during lesson-plan preparation. Participants were asked to choose one or more mathematics curriculum outcomes, prepare a lesson plan using ChatGPT, and then respond to an open-ended questionnaire. The qualitative analysis focused on the purposes for which ChatGPT was used, including generating activities, problems, examples, evaluation tools, course flow, creative ideas, conceptual explanations, and revisions.

The sample included 56 third-year pre-service middle school mathematics teachers at a state university in Turkey. The study was conducted in the spring semester of the 2023–2024 academic year. Findings showed that ChatGPT was used mainly to create lesson content, especially learning activities, problems/examples, assessment tools, and course flow, and secondarily to deepen pedagogical and conceptual knowledge. The author concludes that ChatGPT can be a useful support tool in teacher education for lesson planning, but it should complement, not replace, teachers' expertise, and its outputs should be checked carefully for accuracy.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative phenomenological study using convenience sampling and open-ended questionnaire data with content analysis. It provides useful descriptive evidence, but it does not estimate causal impact and has limited generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical usefulness of ChatGPT for teacher lesson planning, but it does not measure student learning gains or quantify impact. The evidence indicates potential benefits for planning efficiency and teacher cognition, but the impact on educational outcomes remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: Pre-service middle school mathematics teachers used ChatGPT to support lesson plan development, including generating activities, problems, examples, assessment tools, course flow, creative ideas, concept explanations, and revisions.

finding.finding_summary: This qualitative phenomenological study (n=56 pre-service middle school mathematics teachers) found that ChatGPT was widely used to speed and structure lesson-plan development. Participants reported using it to generate course flow, activities, problems, assessments, and revisions, suggesting improved planning efficiency, but no quantitative effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Self-reported uses/purposes of ChatGPT in lesson plan development from open-ended questionnaire responses

finding.finding_summary: The study found that ChatGPT supported durable skills such as creativity, idea generation, and pedagogical problem-solving during lesson planning. Pre-service teachers reported that it helped them think of novel activities, connect concepts, and deepen their own pedagogical and conceptual understanding; however, the evidence is qualitative and descriptive with no effect size reported.
finding.measure: Self-reported pedagogical idea generation, conceptual understanding, and lesson-plan revision purposes
